transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-14 08:00 PDT / 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes (recording started a minute into the call)
Attendees: Avery (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Priya (CSM), Samira (VeraHealth EngM), Jon (VeraHealth SRE), Luca (VeraHealth CTO), Maya (VeraHealth Security)
Links shared: https://redwood.app/notes/incident-342, https://drive.company/verahealth/incident-342-logs (customer), internal: https://redwood.internal/patch/342

Summary (auto): quick closure sync after last week's production latency cascade. Confirmed patch plan, verification steps, and next steps for rollforward/rollback and updated runbooks. Discussed K V cache corruption hypothesis and telemetry gaps. Agreed on staged smoke runs and final release window.

Topics: root cause hypothesis, patch contents and mitigations, verification plan, telemetry improvements, stakeholder comms, security signoff

Transcript body:
[00:00] Avery: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. I know we have a tight scope — the recording started a bit late so we'll keep notes concise. Um, Diego do you want to lead the tech summary?
[00:20] Diego: Yeah, quick recap. Last Wednesday we saw a progressive latency increase that culminated in a cascade when the KV cache started thrashing. Our working hypothesis is a rebalancer edge-case that caused duplicate cache invalidations which then induced a lock contention on the shard leader. This increased token latency and ultimately caused retries that hit our autoscaler and overloaded the dedicated pool.
[00:45] Samira: Sorry can I just pause — when you say duplicate invalidations you mean multiple invalidation messages for the same key got processed?
[00:52] Diego: Exactly, like the same prefix eviction came in concurrently. Also there's a note that the K-V cash metrics were sampled at one minute granularity, so short bursts were invisible. (laugh) transcription sometimes writes K V cash, but it's KV cache.
[01:10] Jon: And that sampling gap is crucial — we missed the pre-failure spike because the metric rollup smoothed it out. On our side we also saw a gap in audit log pickup for about 4 minutes between our collector and the ingestion pipeline.
[01:30] Luca: We need to understand whether this is systemic or a rare timing window. Our concern is recurrence during higher peak loads.
[01:38] Diego: Agreed. The patch we're proposing has three parts: 1) guardrails on the rebalancer to dedupe invalidations, 2) lowering the KV cache sampling window to 10s for critical metrics, and 3) a small change to the shard leader lock to reduce contention under bursts.
[01:58] Maya: From a security/compliance angle, any rollout needs audit log continuity and no change to encryption-at-rest or KMS usage.
[02:06] Avery: Yep, we'll keep KMS unchanged. Priya can you run through the customer communications plan?
[02:15] Priya: We'll send an updated postmortem and the remediation timeline. We're recommending an evening rollout with a 1-hour verification hold and a fallback window if errors exceed threshold. Also we'll include the new runbook snippets for SRE playbooks.
[02:35] Samira: For the smoke runs, can you spell out what you want us to exercise? We have separate teams for inference load and traffic shaping.
[02:44] Diego: Two parallel tests: one is a synthetic inference load that mirrors P95 token lengths and burst patterns; second is a chaos-ish run where we stress the rebalancer with simulated shard movements. We want artifact logs: KV eviction traces, leader lock contention traces, and full token timing histograms.
[03:10] Jon: On the chaos run — we need the exact sequence so we can script it. Can Diego or someone drop a step-by-step?
[03:17] Diego: I'll post a script in the ticket; it's basically: trigger controlled shard move, fire N concurrent invalidations for a target prefix, and run 10x normal inference QPS for 5 minutes. We'll parameterize the N and QPS so you can step it up.
[03:35] Samira: Great. Also, regarding the autoscaler noise that amplified the problem: what short-term mitigations are you suggesting?
[03:42] Diego: Two things short-term: tweak autoscale cooldowns to be more conservative for the dedicated pool (we'll share exact yaml), and enable a temporary capacity buffer so spikes don't cause immediate elastic allocations during verification.
[04:05] Luca: Can we get numbers? How much buffer?
[04:07] Diego: Suggest +20% reserved headroom for the dedicated pool during business hours; we can dial that down after we validate.
[04:15] Maya: Do we need any SOC2 re-approval for the guardrail change? I know SOC2 covers controls but not feature-level code changes typically.
[04:24] Avery: We will share the updated change summary and our SOC2 artifacts; typically no re-cert required, but we can flag anything that touches access controls. This change is algorithmic and doesn't alter auth/KMS.
[04:40] Jon: One more thing — during the incident our fallback routes didn't trigger because the model variant mapping table hadn't synced. That was a config propagation lag. Can we make propagation more atomic?
[04:52] Diego: We're exploring atomic config apply for the model routing table; immediate mitigation is to shorten TTL and add a scraper that validates mapping sync before traffic shift. We'll include that in the patch bundle.
[05:10] Samira: That sounds good. On verification, what telemetry thresholds will you use to mark the rollout successful?
[05:18] Diego: We'll define success as: P95 token latency within 10% of baseline for 30 minutes, error rate under 0.1% on inference endpoints, KV cache eviction rate stable and no lock contention spikes. We'll provide dashboards for you to monitor.
[05:40] Priya: We'll also include automated alert rules and a short-run checklist so your oncall knows what to watch for.
[05:48] Luca: How long will the patch window be? We prefer a short window during off-peak.
[05:54] Avery: We're targeting a 90-minute maintenance window with a 60-minute verification hold. If anything breaches thresholds, immediate rollback plan to previous model shard config is available.
[06:10] Jon: Rollback time estimate?
[06:12] Diego: ~12-15 minutes to revert config and traffic; full warmup maybe 10 more minutes depending on cache cold start.
[06:20] Samira: Regarding cache cold starts — will the fallback increase token cost temporarily? We care about both latency and cost bump for the business case.
[06:28] Diego: Yes, cold cache can increase per-token compute. We'll provide an estimate based on your observed token distribution; worst-case a 15-25% cost increase for 30 minutes. We'll include cost mitigation tips, like temporarily lowering max request length for non-critical endpoints through routing rules.
[06:50] Maya: Also want the audit log ingestion continuity verified — who owns that?
[06:55] Jon: VeraHealth side owns the collector but we need Redwood to confirm the ingestion pipeline will accept the events with the new sampling cadence.
[07:05] Diego: We'll validate ingestion path end-to-end and share a short verification script.
[07:12] Samira: Ok good. Anything on the long-term?
[07:16] Diego: Long-term: rework rebalancer to avoid duplicate invalidation paths, permanent finer-grain metrics for cache, and improved atomic config propagation. We propose a Q2 engineering ticket set with milestone checkpoints.
[07:30] Luca: And are we still on track for the SLA credit discussion? We want fairness but not an overcomplicated back-and-forth.
[07:40] Avery: Priya will lead SLA credit talks; we can scope it based on measurable impact and include that in the postmortem.
[07:50] Priya: I'll draft a proposal and share by Thursday.
[08:00] Jon: A few quick clarifications: the collector gap — was it due to backpressure or a config rotate?
[08:07] Diego: Preliminary root cause suggests the collector process dropped a batch during a config reload on the ingestion tier. We're adding a graceful reload and queue drain to the ingestion service.
[08:20] Samira: Any impact to encryption keys or tokenization?
[08:24] Avery: No for this change. Keys/KMS unaffected.
[08:28] Maya: Good. Please include the pen-test summary as well — we need that for our compliance board to sign off on the patch.
[08:36] Avery: Will do, link in the ticket.
[08:40] Diego: I'll attach the smoke test scripts and a parameterized chaos script.
[08:45] Samira: We'll run two 24-hour smoke runs starting Friday night; if they pass we'll schedule the maintenance window the following week.
[08:55] Priya: Recap: Redwood shares patch and runbook by Friday 2026-04-16; VeraHealth runs smoke runs and shares logs by 2026-04-19; follow-up call week of 2026-04-20.
[09:10] Luca: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[09:12] Avery: Thanks all, we appreciate the collaboration. We'll keep channels open on the ticket and Slack #vera-incident-342.
[09:20] (call ends)
